-- A 2-entry pipeline FIFO. `deq` runs first, then `enq`: enq sees the slot
-- that deq just freed, so even a full FIFO accepts an item in the cycle it
-- delivers one. Both rules write count, so they are chained, not parallel.
xblue module mkPipeFifo2;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bool enq_valid;
  input Bit#(8) enq_data;
  input Bool deq_ready;

  Reg#(Vector#(2, Bit#(8))) data <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(1)) wp <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(1)) rp <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(2)) count <- mkReg(0);

  -- what the caller sees at the start of the cycle
  method Bool    enq_ready = count != 2 || deq_ready;
  method Bool    deq_valid = count != 0;
  method Bit#(8) deq_data  = data[rp];

  rule deq (deq_ready && count != 0);
    rp <= rp + 1;
    count <= count - 1;
  endrule

  -- count is read after deq has run: a full FIFO has room again
  rule enq (enq_valid && count != 2);
    data[wp] <= enq_data;
    wp <= wp + 1;
    count <= count + 1;
  endrule

  rule clear (reset);
    wp <= 0;
    rp <= 0;
    count <= 0;
  endrule

  schedule deq ≫ enq ≫ clear;
endmodule

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

structure Regs where
  data : BitVec 16
  wp : BitVec 1
  rp : BitVec 1
  count : BitVec 2

/-- One clock cycle of the design itself: the registers after it, and the three outputs. -/
def run (reset enq : BitVec 1) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) :
    Regs × BitVec 1 × BitVec 1 × BitVec 8 :=
  let t := mkPipeFifo2.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons enq (.cons x (.cons deq .nil))))
              (.cons s.data (.cons s.wp (.cons s.rp (.cons s.count .nil))))
  (⟨t.regs.get mkPipeFifo2.data, t.regs.get mkPipeFifo2.wp, t.regs.get mkPipeFifo2.rp,
    t.regs.get mkPipeFifo2.count⟩, t.wires.get mkPipeFifo2.enq_ready,
    t.wires.get mkPipeFifo2.deq_valid, t.wires.get mkPipeFifo2.deq_data)

/-- Slot `i` of the packed vector. -/
def slot (d : BitVec 16) (i : BitVec 1) : BitVec 8 := if i = 0#1 then d.extractLsb' 0 8 else d.extractLsb' 8 8

/-- The queue the registers stand for: `count` items, starting at `rp`. -/
def abs (s : Regs) : List (BitVec 8) :=
  (List.range s.count.toNat).map fun i => slot s.data (s.rp + BitVec.ofNat 1 i)

/-- The cycle as a story on a list: first `deq`, then `enq`, which sees the
    queue `deq` left. -/
def spec (q : List (BitVec 8)) (enq : Bool) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : Bool) : List (BitVec 8) × Bool :=
  let deqFire := deq && !q.isEmpty
  let q1 := if deqFire then q.tail else q            -- deq
  let enqRdy := decide (q1.length < 2)
  (if enq && enqRdy then q1 ++ [x] else q1, enqRdy)   -- enq

/-- count <= 2, and the pointers agree with it. -/
def Inv (s : Regs) : Prop := s.count ≤ 2#2 ∧ s.wp = s.rp + s.count.setWidth 1

theorem pipeline_correct (s : Regs) (hinv : Inv s) (enq : BitVec 1) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) :
    let r := run 0#1 enq x deq s
    abs r.1 = (spec (abs s) (enq = 1#1) x (deq = 1#1)).1 ∧
    (r.2.1 = 1#1 ↔ (spec (abs s) (enq = 1#1) x (deq = 1#1)).2 = true) ∧
    (r.2.2.1 = 1#1 ↔ abs s ≠ []) ∧ (abs s ≠ [] → r.2.2.2 = (abs s).head!) ∧ Inv r.1 := by
  obtain ⟨d, wp, rp, c⟩ := s
  simp only [Inv] at hinv
  simp [run, abs, spec, slot, mkPipeFifo2.design, Design.cycle, mkPipeFifo2.schedule,
    mkPipeFifo2.interfaces, mkPipeFifo2.rules.deq, mkPipeFifo2.rules.enq, mkPipeFifo2.rules.clear,
    mkPipeFifo2.signature, Sched.run, Action.step, Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur,
    State.read, HList.set, HList.get, Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, Common.putR, Common.putW,
    Common.memAt, Common.zeros, mkPipeFifo2.data, mkPipeFifo2.wp, mkPipeFifo2.rp, mkPipeFifo2.count,
    mkPipeFifo2.reset, mkPipeFifo2.enq_valid, mkPipeFifo2.enq_data, mkPipeFifo2.deq_ready,
    mkPipeFifo2.enq_ready, mkPipeFifo2.deq_valid, mkPipeFifo2.deq_data, sliceWidth]
  have bit : ∀ v : BitVec 1, v = 0#1 ∨ v = 1#1 := by decide
  have cnt : ∀ v : BitVec 2, v ≤ 2#2 → v = 0#2 ∨ v = 1#2 ∨ v = 2#2 := by decide
  obtain ⟨hc, hw⟩ := hinv
  rcases cnt c hc with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit rp with rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit enq with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases bit deq with rfl | rfl <;> simp at hw <;> subst hw <;> simp [Inv, List.range_succ] <;> try bv_decide

theorem abs_length (s : Regs) : (abs s).length = s.count.toNat := by simp [abs]

/-- The point of a pipeline FIFO: a full queue that delivers an item this cycle
    also accepts one, and the queue is the old one without its head, plus `x`. -/
theorem full_accepts_while_delivering (s : Regs) (hinv : Inv s) (hfull : s.count = 2#2) (x : BitVec 8) :
    let r := run 0#1 1#1 x 1#1 s
    r.2.1 = 1#1 ∧ abs r.1 = (abs s).tail ++ [x] := by
  have h := pipeline_correct s hinv 1#1 x 1#1
  have hl : (abs s).length = 2 := by simp [abs_length, hfull]
  have hne : abs s ≠ [] := by intro h; simp [h] at hl
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := h
  simp [spec, hl, hne] at h1 h2
  exact ⟨h2, h1⟩

/-- An empty queue refuses a dequeue: it is not valid. -/
theorem empty_has_nothing (s : Regs) (hinv : Inv s) (hempty : s.count = 0#2) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) :
    (run 0#1 0#1 x deq s).2.2.1 = 0#1 := by
  have h := (pipeline_correct s hinv 0#1 x deq).2.2.1
  have hl : abs s = [] := by simp [abs, hempty]
  have hz : ¬ (run 0#1 0#1 x deq s).2.2.1 = 1#1 := by simpa [hl] using h
  have bit : ∀ v : BitVec 1, ¬ v = 1#1 → v = 0#1 := by decide
  exact bit _ hz

explain: With enq ≫ deq, the story reads the other way round: enq first (it sees the queue as it was, so a full queue refuses), then deq, which sees the queue enq left. That is a bypass FIFO. spec is the same two steps in the new order, deq_valid becomes q1 non-empty, and bypass_correct proves the design refines it. The methods have to look at the incoming item (deq_valid = count != 0 || enq_valid, deq_data = count == 0 ? enq_data : data[rp]), because they are computed from the start-of-cycle state. empty_passes_through is the new fact: an empty queue with a ready consumer is valid, delivers x, and is empty again. The pipeline FIFO's full_accepts_while_delivering is false in this order: a full queue refuses. In the simulation, the first cycle shows it: the FIFO is empty, enq_valid and deq_ready are both high, and deq_valid and deq_data show the item 5 in the cycle it goes in; the FIFO is empty again afterwards.

explain: The registers' reset value is all zeros, and the all-zero state has count = 0 and wp = rp, so the invariant holds and the queue it stands for is empty. After a reset cycle the clear rule writes the same three registers, so the machine is back in this state. Together with pipeline_correct (which keeps the invariant) every reachable state satisfies it.

/-- The cycle as a story on a list: first `deq`, then `enq`, which sees the
    queue `deq` left. -/
def spec (q : List (BitVec 8)) (enq : Bool) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : Bool) : List (BitVec 8) × Bool :=
  let deqFire := deq && !q.isEmpty
  let q1 := if deqFire then q.tail else q            -- deq
  let enqRdy := decide (q1.length < 2)
  (if enq && enqRdy then q1 ++ [x] else q1, enqRdy)   -- enq

/-- count <= 2, and the pointers agree with it. -/
def Inv (s : Regs) : Prop := s.count ≤ 2#2 ∧ s.wp = s.rp + s.count.setWidth 1

theorem pipeline_correct (s : Regs) (hinv : Inv s) (enq : BitVec 1) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) :
    let r := run 0#1 enq x deq s
    abs r.1 = (spec (abs s) (enq = 1#1) x (deq = 1#1)).1 ∧
    (r.2.1 = 1#1 ↔ (spec (abs s) (enq = 1#1) x (deq = 1#1)).2 = true) ∧
    (r.2.2.1 = 1#1 ↔ abs s ≠ []) ∧ (abs s ≠ [] → r.2.2.2 = (abs s).head!) ∧ Inv r.1 := by
  obtain ⟨d, wp, rp, c⟩ := s
  simp only [Inv] at hinv
  simp [run, abs, spec, slot, mkPipeFifo2.design, Design.cycle, mkPipeFifo2.schedule,
    mkPipeFifo2.interfaces, mkPipeFifo2.rules.deq, mkPipeFifo2.rules.enq, mkPipeFifo2.rules.clear,
    mkPipeFifo2.signature, Sched.run, Action.step, Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur,
    State.read, HList.set, HList.get, Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Expr.cmpVal, Common.putR, Common.putW,
    Common.memAt, Common.zeros, mkPipeFifo2.data, mkPipeFifo2.wp, mkPipeFifo2.rp, mkPipeFifo2.count,
    mkPipeFifo2.reset, mkPipeFifo2.enq_valid, mkPipeFifo2.enq_data, mkPipeFifo2.deq_ready,
    mkPipeFifo2.enq_ready, mkPipeFifo2.deq_valid, mkPipeFifo2.deq_data, sliceWidth]
  have bit : ∀ v : BitVec 1, v = 0#1 ∨ v = 1#1 := by decide
  have cnt : ∀ v : BitVec 2, v ≤ 2#2 → v = 0#2 ∨ v = 1#2 ∨ v = 2#2 := by decide
  obtain ⟨hc, hw⟩ := hinv
  rcases cnt c hc with rfl | rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit rp with rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit enq with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases bit deq with rfl | rfl <;> simp at hw <;> subst hw <;> simp [Inv, List.range_succ] <;> try bv_decide

/-- The all-zero registers satisfy the invariant: reset starts the FIFO empty. -/
theorem reset_inv : Inv ⟨0#16, 0#1, 0#1, 0#2⟩ ∧ abs ⟨0#16, 0#1, 0#1, 0#2⟩ = [] := by
  simp [Inv, abs]

theorem abs_length (s : Regs) : (abs s).length = s.count.toNat := by simp [abs]

/-- The point of a pipeline FIFO: a full queue that delivers an item this cycle
    also accepts one, and the queue is the old one without its head, plus `x`. -/
theorem full_accepts_while_delivering (s : Regs) (hinv : Inv s) (hfull : s.count = 2#2) (x : BitVec 8) :
    let r := run 0#1 1#1 x 1#1 s
    r.2.1 = 1#1 ∧ abs r.1 = (abs s).tail ++ [x] := by
  have h := pipeline_correct s hinv 1#1 x 1#1
  have hl : (abs s).length = 2 := by simp [abs_length, hfull]
  have hne : abs s ≠ [] := by intro h; simp [h] at hl
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := h
  simp [spec, hl, hne] at h1 h2
  exact ⟨h2, h1⟩

/-- An empty queue refuses a dequeue: it is not valid. -/
theorem empty_has_nothing (s : Regs) (hinv : Inv s) (hempty : s.count = 0#2) (x : BitVec 8) (deq : BitVec 1) :
    (run 0#1 0#1 x deq s).2.2.1 = 0#1 := by
  have h := (pipeline_correct s hinv 0#1 x deq).2.2.1
  have hl : abs s = [] := by simp [abs, hempty]
  have hz : ¬ (run 0#1 0#1 x deq s).2.2.1 = 1#1 := by simpa [hl] using h
  have bit : ∀ v : BitVec 1, ¬ v = 1#1 → v = 0#1 := by decide
  exact bit _ hz
